labelled_by: one person, one pass; no second labeller

labels.note: Read of a PNG in the scratchpad, 77 -> 92, nothing wrote to it in between. A screenshot file the agent itself produced and then read twice; the second read returned the same 29 KB and could not have returned anything else.

Rubric 3b. `Stop-Process` on whatever is listening on port 3100, guarded by `if ($c)`. It prints `stopped` whether or not anything was running -- the identical output is what an idempotent command does. Asserting a state, not asking a question.
Same command as [2], 73 calls apart. Same reasoning.
Same command as [2], 103 calls apart. Same reasoning.

`vercel --prod --yes` twice, 4 calls apart. A deploy is a state assertion by rubric 3b, but this one pipes through `tail -6` and the identical tail could mean either a real second deploy or a no-op. The trace does not show which, and the rubric forbids guessing.

`make 2>&1`, 121 -> 182, with 60 calls in between including four other builds and edits to the sources. A rebuild is a check on work done since the last one; identical output means nothing broke, which is the information the agent wanted. Rubric 3a.
Read of `database.hpp`, 4 -> 18, 13 calls in between and nothing wrote to it. The second read could not have returned anything new.
Read of `~routes.generated.ts`, 26 -> 31, 4 calls in between, no write to it. Same file, same bytes, four calls apart.

Write of identical content to `~routes.generated.ts`, 36 -> 63, with a Write of the same content in between. ★ A Write's output is a fixed confirmation naming the path, so identical output here says nothing about whether the work repeated -- see the results note. Whether regenerating a file that came out the same was wasted depends on whether the generator's inputs changed, which the trace does not show.

Read of a password-protected PDF, 230 -> 231, adjacent calls, nothing in between. The first call returned 'PDF is password-protected'; the second asked the same question one call later and got the same sentence. Nothing could have changed.
A `clang` build line, 69 -> 88, 18 calls in between including another build of the same target. Rebuilding after work is a check. Rubric 3a.
Same build command as [11], 101 calls apart, eight builds in between. Same reasoning.

Piping a Prolog program into `epilog.exe`, 108 -> 256, 147 calls in between. Running the built binary again after 147 calls of work on it is how the agent finds out whether the build still behaves. Rubric 3a.
Read of `main.py`, 6 -> 62, 55 calls in between, no write to it. A 222-byte file read twice across most of the session.
Read of `storage.py`, 35 -> 79, 43 calls in between, no write to it.
Read of `limiter.py`, 38 -> 87. The six 'same target' hits are Grep calls whose `path` is the project root and match only as a string prefix -- none of them wrote anything. No write to the file.
Read of `stripe_wrapper/__init__.py`, 32 -> 61, returning 'File does not exist' both times, 28 calls apart, with nothing creating it. Asking twice whether a file exists that nobody made.
Read of `slack_api/_http.py`, 38 -> 54, 15 calls in between, no write.
Read of `message_sent_webhook.py`, 20 -> 59. The one 'touching' call is a Glob for `**/middleware*`, which reads and matched only by prefix.
Read of `notion-proxy/proxy.py`, 24 -> 91, 66 calls apart. The ten 'touching' calls are all Glob patterns against the project root.
Read of `logging_config.py`, 11 -> 14, two calls in between, no write.
Read of `permissions.py`, 34 -> 52. The 'touching' call is a Glob for `**/serializers.py`, a different file.
Read of `views.py`, 32 -> 58. Two Glob calls in between, neither wrote.
Read of `log_etl_pipeline.py`, 21 -> 35. The 'touching' call is a Grep for 'elas...' across the project; it read, it did not write.
Read of `requirements.txt`, 10 -> 37, 26 calls apart. Same Grep as [24] in between; nothing wrote to the file.
Read of `analyze_parquet.py`, 16 -> 50. Ten Glob/Grep hits against the project root, none of them writes.
Read of `test_aho_corasick.py`, 25 -> 52, 26 calls in between, no write to it.
Read of `etl_pipeline.py`, 26 -> 51, 24 calls in between, no write.
Read of `requirements.txt`, 5 -> 31. Three Grep calls in between, all reads.
`Glob **/MythosMini/**` twice, 6 -> 7, adjacent, returning 'No files found' both times. Nothing happened in between and nothing could create a match.
